sources.text:
Miss North Carolina USA stripped of title; Miss USA CEO condemns 'racism,' 'homophobia' and 'transphobia'
Weeks ahead of the 75th annual Miss USA pageant, Miss North Carolina USA 2026, Brittany Boltinhouse, has been stripped of her crown, and the runner-up will now assume the title.
In a post on social media announcing that Boltinhouse's "reign as Miss North Carolina USA 2026 came to an end," Miss USA CEO Thom Brodeur didn't specify what alleged conduct resulted in the decision to strip her of her title. However, Brodeur said the organization "does not tolerate racism, homophobia, transphobia, nor language that strips any person of their dignity — whoever they are."
Brodeur said the decision to strip Boltinhouse of her title was made in coordination with Boltinhouse, state directors in North Carolina, and "in consultation with the Miss USA organization."
Brodeur said Boltinhouse was expected to release a statement "soon," but said he wanted to "speak to the issue plainly, because our titleholders, our state directors, fans and every young woman watching deserves to hear where I stand."
After saying the Miss USA organization condemns "racism," "homophobia," and "transphobia," Brodeur added, "that is not a policy written for a press release. It is the floor of what it means to represent the brand."
"A title here isn't a trinket. It is a position of trust, extended by an organization and accepted by a woman who agrees to carry a standard in public," the Miss USA CEO said. "When that standard is broken, the title cannot continue as though nothing happened."
A Blaize Productions, which runs pageants in the Carolinas, released the following statement, in part, on social media:
"After careful consideration, multiple conversations, and in consultation with the Miss USA Organization, A Blaize Productions has made the difficult decision to conclude Brittany Boltinhouse’s reign as Miss North Carolina USA 2026.
"This decision was not made lightly. It followed a thorough review of recently surfaced information and was based on the totality of the circumstances and our responsibility to preserve the integrity of the Miss North Carolina USA title and the values of our organization."
First-runner up Myla Hadley will represent North Carolina at upcoming pageant
Blaize Productions didn't elaborate on the "recently surfaced information. That organization said Myla Hadley, first runner-up, will represent North Carolina at the pageant later this month.
"We have every confidence that she will represent North Carolina with grace, professionalism, and dedication as she prepares for Miss USA," the organization said of Hadley.
In a post to her Instagram story, Hadley, wrote, "Thank you to everyone for all the support and love you've shown me throughout this entire process. I am extremely grateful and humbled by all the encouraging messages and the support I've received."
Hadley continued, saying, "I understand the seriousness and level of prestige that this title carries," and that she and her team "are ready to take this on."
The Miss USA pageant is slated to take place in Miami, Florida, on Aug. 27.
"While this may seem like a two-week turnaround given the circumstances, I've been preparing to represent at Miss USA since I first competed with this organization," Hadley said. "I am ready to represent North Carolina. Thank you all again for your motivation and well wishes."
Read Blaize Productions' full statement
"At A Blaize Productions, our mission has always been to empower women to lead with integrity, courage, accountability, and purpose. We believe that people are capable of growth, that grace and accountability can coexist, and that one mistake does not have to define an entire life.
We also believe that leadership carries a unique responsibility. As an organization entrusted with selecting and preparing women to represent our states on the national stage, we must uphold the standards and values that our titleholders agree to embrace when accepting the honor of wearing the crown.
After careful consideration, multiple conversations, and in consultation with the Miss USA Organization, A Blaize Productions has made the difficult decision to conclude Brittany Boltinhouse’s reign as Miss North Carolina USA 2026.
This decision was not made lightly. It followed a thorough review of recently surfaced information and was based on the totality of the circumstances and our responsibility to preserve the integrity of the Miss North Carolina USA title and the values of our organization.
We recognize the hard work Brittany invested in earning the title and sincerely thank her for the time, dedication, and commitment she gave throughout this process. We wish her nothing but the very best as she moves forward.
In accordance with our succession procedures, Myla Hadley, First Runner-Up, will assume the title of Miss North Carolina USA 2026. We have every confidence that she will represent North Carolina with grace, professionalism, and dedication as she prepares for Miss USA.
We ask our pageant family, supporters, and the public to extend kindness and respect to both Brittany and Myla during this transition. Moments like these are never easy for anyone involved, and we remain committed to treating everyone with dignity while continuing our mission of empowering the next generation of women leaders." 
___
Carrie Hodgin with sister station WXII contributed to this report

Thom Brodeur, chairman and CEO of Miss USA and Miss Teen USA, posted a statement on Instagram describing conduct that broke the organization’s standards, without specifying the exact conduct. This comes after the Miss American Fork 2024 winner died "unexpectedly."
He wrote that the organization “does not tolerate racism, homophobia, transphobia nor language that strips any person of their dignity — whoever they are.”
“That is not a policy written for a press release,” Brodeur wrote. “It is the floor of what it means to represent this brand.”
He continued to emphasize the standards and responsibility that come with winning a title from the Miss USA Organization.
“A title here isn’t a trinket,” he wrote. “It is a position of trust, extended by an organization and accepted by a woman who agrees to carry a standard in public. When that standard is broken, the title cannot continue as though nothing happened.”
Without naming the exact incident, Brodeur said, “What was brought to us was not a single moment. It reflected conduct over an extended period of time. That is why this outcome was reached, and I stand behind it without qualification.”
He noted that “state titleholders are recruited, vetted, and approved for competition at the state level” and that the organization “acted as soon as this reached us.”
He continued to urge people with the reminder, “There is a young woman at the center of this.”
“She has been named, examined, and judged in public in a way that most of us would not survive, and she is still a human being with a family, a future, and a life ahead of her that is longer than this part of her journey,” he wrote.
“I have never believed that accountability requires cruelty, or that holding a line means enjoying the fall of the person who crossed it,” his statement continued.
He underscored that “zero tolerance is a standard for conduct,” but it is “not permission to strip someone of their humanity.”
Brodeur explained that Boltinhouse will be releasing her own statement that includes “ownership, accountability, and apology.”
“While it does not undo the harm, and it does not change the outcome, it is the beginning of the only thing that ever repairs harm, which is change,” he noted, regarding her forthcoming statement.
Brodeur wrapped up his statement by offering well wishes for Boltinhouse’s future and announcing who would take her place.
Who will become Miss North Carolina 2026?
Brodeur announced that Myla Hadley, as the first runner-up in the competition, will be taking over the title of Miss North Carolina 2026, noting that she has the organization’s “full confidence and our support.”
She released her own statement on her Instagram Stories, writing, “Thank you to everyone for all the support and love you’ve shown me throughout this entire process. I am extremely grateful and humbled by all the encouraging messages and the support I’ve received. I understand the seriousness and level of prestige that this title carries, and I can confidently say that both my team and I are ready to take this on.”
Hadley will represent the state in the upcoming 75th annual Miss USA pageant, taking place later this month in Miami, Florida.

Brittany Boltinhouse is a 27-year-old North Carolina pageant contestant who was crowned Miss North Carolina USA on June 28. She is originally from Duplin County and currently lives in Leland, North Carolina.
Her victory was widely celebrated, with reports noting she became the first Honduran titleholder to win Miss North Carolina USA. She had been preparing to compete at the Miss USA pageant later this month before the title was revoked.

Pageant organizers did not initially specify the exact issue that led to Boltinhouse's removal, saying only that the decision followed a "thorough review" of newly surfaced information.

The posts reportedly included repeated use of the N-word, prompting criticism after screenshots resurfaced online. Some outlets have also reported allegations that additional posts contained homophobic and transphobic language, although pageant organizers have not publicly released the posts themselves.

Did Brittany Boltinhouse Support Trump?

One post reportedly warned that electing Kamala Harris would turn the U.S. into a "third world country," while another expressed support for Trump.
Some social media users have attempted to link the controversy to Boltinhouse's political views, but there is no public evidence that she lost her title because of support for Trump or any political affiliation.
The statements released by A Blaize Productions and the Miss USA Organization focused exclusively on the resurfaced social media posts and whether they violated the organization's standards regarding racism and discriminatory language.
